question: Can cross-image transfer of fine-tuning-specific conditioning responses improve patient membership auditing and the comparison of protection, utility and cost?

access.primary: white-box target weights plus public pre-finetuning base

scenarios.E: all observed member images in the training manifest
scenarios.U: all observed images excluded from training; other images of the patient included

candidate.name: cross-image conditioning response transfer, provisional
candidate.fold_rule: hash partition; swapped support/query; weight by query count
candidate.optimization: projected normalized gradient ascent on mean base loss minus target loss
candidate.control_matching: target-independent public encoder; different patients; no membership or attack-score selection
candidate.control_bank_rule: separate public nonmember bank, excluded from target and shadow training
candidate.score: query held-out response gain minus matched-other-patient gain, averaged over swapped folds
unresolved_before_execution: basis token and padding mask details
exact power by m and overlap scenario

calibration.assumption: exchangeable nonmember patient bags within the declared evaluation population
calibration.thesis_extension_proposal: hash reserve one third of the frozen nonmember cohort for CVPR calibration before outcomes; preserve original thesis primary analysis

stages.task: feature adapters, probe and cost ledger implementation
minimum two public-development non-DP LoRA models with controlled inclusion
strong-baseline comparison, independent pilot testing and method freeze
existing thesis K5 utility feasibility and K10 matrix
frozen CVPR extension on shared K10 checkpoints
matched patient-budget privacy, utility, cost and reuse comparison

protection.primary_budget_match: M1-G8 versus M2-P8 under their K-specific patient accounting targets

stop_conditions: no additional membership signal beyond strong baselines
same gain from MoFit transfer or standard linear/set statistics
gain attributable to source, anatomy or uncontrolled inclusion confounds
gain disappears under matched patient FPR and compute
unseen-image claim unsupported by scenario U
